summary: 14-day analysis reveals excellent Time in Range (86.0%) but an elevated hypoglycemia burden (5.1% TBR), concentrated overnight (23:00-04:00) and in the early evening (18:00-20:00). Zero logged carb entries indicate complete reliance on Unannounced Meal (UAM) handling and dynamic ISF. Highly permissive safety limits (max IOB 25 U, max basal 12 U/h against ~19.7 U TDI) allow aggressive late SMB stacking following afternoon meal spikes, driving subsequent evening and nocturnal drops.

analysis_steps.findings: Excellent CGM coverage (98.7% over 14 days, cadence 5.0 min, largest gap 65 min). Active AAPS profile and loop statuses present. Zero carb treatment entries logged (total carbs 0.0 g), indicating full unannounced meal (UAM) execution.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid CGM entries, 2,315 treatments (655 insulin entries totaling 275.95 U insulin), 0 carb entries.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of recorded carbohydrate entries prevents direct mathematical isolation of Carb Ratios (CR) without UAM interference.

analysis_steps.findings: Mean glucose is 121.6 mg/dL with CV of 32.6% and TIR of 86.0%. Total Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL) is 5.1%, exceeding the clinical target of <4.0%. Recurrent low glucose occurs overnight (00:00-04:00 TBR 10.1-18.5%) and early evening (19:00 TBR 15.3%), with extreme lows dropping to 41-42 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.evidence: Glucose extremes of 41-42 mg/dL on Aug 13, Aug 14, and Aug 21. Hourly local TBR peaks at 18.5% at 01:00 and 15.3% at 19:00.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of carb entries hides fast-acting carbohydrate rescue interventions from loop calculations.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight target of 90 mg/dL provides minimal buffer against IOB. Profile basal 00:00-05:00 (0.6 U/h) is frequently cut to 0 U/h by the loop, indicating baseline over-infusion or lingering postprandial IOB. Evening basal step-up to 0.7 U/h at 19:00 coincides with 15.3% TBR.
analysis_steps.evidence: Target 90 mg/dL from 23:00 to 08:00; loop statuses frequently show low/zero temp basals overnight (e.g. Aug 10 02:46 0 U/h, Aug 16 00:25 0 U/h).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unrecorded meal timing complicates separating true fasting basal needs from postprandial IOB decay.

analysis_steps.findings: Profile ISF is 56 mg/dL/U with Dynamic ISF (70% adjustment factor) active. DIA is set to 10.0 hours. Dynamic ISF aggressively lowers effective ISF down to 27.8-37.9 mg/dL/U during postprandial spikes, driving heavy SMB micro-dosing. GLP-1 therapy (1.25 mg every 3 days) delays gastric emptying, extending carb absorption and exacerbating late SMB stacking.
analysis_steps.evidence: Loop logs show effective ISF reduced to 37.9 mg/dL/U (Aug 19 15:54) and 27.8 mg/dL/U (Aug 21 21:09). GLP-1 1.25 mg notes logged Aug 14, 17, 20.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Missing carb logs prevent direct calculation of true CR values.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are both enabled with smb_always_enabled=true and max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20. Unannounced meals cause insulin delivery to lag carbohydrate absorption by 1-2 hours. Heavy SMB delivery at peak BG creates an insulin tail that causes hypoglycemia 3-5 hours later.
analysis_steps.evidence: Loop enactments demonstrate frequent UAM High Boost and SMB micro-boluses at peak BG (14:00-16:00 TAR 22.6-32.1%), followed by TBR spikes at 18:00-20:00.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits are excessively wide relative to total daily insulin (~19.7 U/day). Max IOB is set to 25.0 U (127% of TDI) and Max Basal is set to 12.0 U/h (15-24x profile basal). These limits fail to constrain runaway SMB stacking during prolonged UAM absorption.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.smb_settings.raw_settings: max_iob_units=25.0, max_basal_u_per_hour=12.0; TDI = 275.95 U / 14 days = 19.7 U/day.

analysis_steps.findings: Absence of prebolusing causes pronounced afternoon glucose rises (13:00-17:00 average 135-163 mg/dL). High BG triggers auto-SMBs which stack and drive evening drops (19:00 TBR 15.3%). Administering meal boluses prior to eating would suppress afternoon peaks and reduce late SMB delivery.
analysis_steps.evidence: Postprandial peak TAR reaches 32.1% at 16:00 local time; correction response windows show glucose drops over 160-175 mg/dL following late afternoon SMB stacks.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of recorded meal times and carb amounts requires inferring meal timing from local hourly glucose profiles.

analysis_steps.findings: Carbohydrate absorption model uses min_5m_carbimpact=8 and meal_max_absorption_hours=7. Delayed gastric emptying from GLP-1 stretches absorption over 4-6 hours. Using e-carbs (extended carbs) for larger meals would allow AAPS to anticipate long absorption tails without relying on aggressive UAM SMB triggers.
analysis_steps.evidence: GLP-1 dosing context on Aug 14, 17, 20; meal_max_absorption_hours=7.0 h in profile settings.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Zero logged carb entries prohibit quantifying actual meal absorption rates.

analysis_steps.findings: The primary clinical issue is excessive hypoglycemia (5.1% TBR) caused by late SMB stacking under unannounced meal conditions, compounded by dangerously high safety limit ceilings (max IOB 25 U). Order of intervention: 1) Restructure AAPS safety limits immediately to cap maximum automated insulin delivery; 2) Introduce meal carb logging with prebolusing and e-carbs to eliminate afternoon UAM spikes; 3) Re-evaluate baseline profile basal rates once unannounced meal noise is removed.
analysis_steps.evidence: Integrated findings from Checkpoints 1-3. Safety limits (25 U IOB) are disproportionate to TDI (19.7 U). Over 80% of low glucose events follow reactive UAM SMB stacking.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Requires 5-7 days of active meal carb logging to validate underlying basal and CR parameters accurately.

strengths: High overall Time in Range (86.0%) well above the standard 70% clinical target.
Excellent CGM sensor coverage (98.7%) with minimal data gaps over the 14-day analysis period.
Low average glucose (121.6 mg/dL) demonstrating strong overall glycemic control.
Active open-loop/closed-loop automation successfully preventing severe prolonged hyperglycemia.
issues: Elevated hypoglycemia burden (5.1% TBR) exceeding the standard clinical safety limit of < 4.0%.
Recurrent nocturnal (23:00-04:00) and early evening (18:00-20:00) hypoglycemia with extreme drops to 41-42 mg/dL.
Complete reliance on unannounced meals (0 g carbs logged) leading to delayed insulin delivery and late postprandial SMB stacking.
Excessively high software safety limits (Max IOB 25.0 U, Max Basal 12.0 U/h) relative to Total Daily Insulin (~19.7 U/day).

recommendations.title: Reduce AAPS Max IOB and Max Basal Safety Limits
recommendations.description: The current Max IOB (25 U) represents 127% of total daily insulin (~19.7 U/day) and Max Basal (12 U/h) is 15-24x profile basal rates. Lowering Max IOB to 5.0-6.0 U (~25-30% of TDI) and Max Basal to 3.0 U/h creates a crucial safety guardrail against runaway insulin stacking.

recommendations.title: Transition from Unannounced Meals to Meal Carb Bolusing
recommendations.description: Log meal carbs and bolus 10-15 minutes prior to eating. Replacing UAM delivery with upfront boluses suppresses afternoon glucose spikes (14:00-16:00 TAR 22-32%) and prevents reactive SMB stacking that drives 19:00 hypoglycemia.

recommendations.title: Raise Overnight Glucose Target Buffer
recommendations.description: An overnight target of 90 mg/dL provides little safety margin during sleep. Raising the target to 100 mg/dL from 23:00 to 08:00 reduces nocturnal hypoglycemia risk (10-18% TBR) while baseline data is collected.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep current profile basal, CR, ISF, and target segments unchanged while updating AAPS safety limits and introducing meal carb entries.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Profile adjustments should not be made while unannounced meal noise and excessive safety limit ceilings drive glycemic variability. Establishing meal carb logging and capping Max IOB will isolate true underlying basal and ISF requirements.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Observe 5-7 days of CGM telemetry after updating safety limits and logging meal carbs to re-evaluate overnight 00:00-05:00 basal stability.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Current limits (25 U IOB, 12 U/h basal) are unsafe for a user requiring ~19.7 U total daily insulin. Lowering Max IOB to 6.0 U (~30% TDI) and Max Basal to 3.0 U/h prevents runaway SMB stacking.
Dynamic ISF at 70% effectively manages high glucose spikes; capping Max IOB provides necessary guardrails without disabling dynamic sensitivity.
7.0 h max absorption aligns well with GLP-1 delayed gastric emptying.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Enter meal carbohydrates into AAPS with a 10-15 minute prebolus prior to eating. For larger or high-fat/protein meals on GLP-1 therapy, split carb entry using e-carbs over 3-4 hours to allow AAPS to predict extended absorption without triggering late UAM SMB stacking.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Prebolusing suppresses afternoon peak TAR (32.1% at 16:00) and eliminates reactive late-afternoon UAM SMB delivery that drives 19:00 hypoglycemia (15.3% TBR).
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log all meal carbs and entry times for 7 consecutive days to measure prebolus effectiveness on postprandial glucose excursions.

exceptions.suggestion: Administer meal bolus at meal start (0 min prebolus) or split into 50% immediate and 50% e-carbs over 2 hours.
exceptions.rationale: Prevents immediate postprandial hypoglycemia when starting from a low baseline.

exceptions.suggestion: Extend e-carb absorption duration to 4-5 hours for main meals.
exceptions.rationale: Matches peak gastrointestinal slowing on GLP-1 administration days.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Discuss lowering AAPS Max IOB to 6.0 U and Max Basal to 3.0 U/h with the care team to establish safe automated delivery limits.
Step 2: Begin entering carbohydrate amounts for all meals into AAPS, applying a 10-15 minute prebolus before eating.
Step 3: Collect 7 days of CGM data with complete meal entries to re-assess postprandial peaks and evening hypoglycemia.
Step 4: Review overnight CGM trends to evaluate whether overnight target (90 mg/dL) or basal (00:00-05:00) requires tuning once postprandial SMB tails are eliminated.
education: Unannounced Meal (UAM) algorithms rely on detecting glucose rises before delivering insulin. In GLP-1 users, delayed digestion causes insulin delivery to occur hours after eating, leading to insulin stacking and late hypoglycemia.
Prebolusing (delivering insulin 10-15 minutes before carbs are consumed) matches insulin peak action to carbohydrate absorption, flattening postprandial spikes.
Max IOB software limits protect against algorithm over-dosing during sensor noise, site issues, or prolonged unannounced meal absorption.
safety_notes: This analysis is decision-support content only and does not constitute medical advice.
All parameter adjustments must be independently verified and approved by the user's healthcare provider.
Settings changes should be implemented one at a time with close glucose monitoring, especially during overnight hours.
